ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The figure shows a Bode magnitude plot, with the vertical axis labeled 20 log|G(j2πf)| and the horizontal axis as logarithmic frequency f(Hz). The curve is approximately a horizontal line of +20 dB in the low-frequency range; then it begins to roll downward near the lower break point; the middle section shows a downward trend of about -20 dB/dec; after the higher break point, it becomes a horizontal line again, stabilizing at about -20 dB. From the readings on the horizontal axis in the figure, the lower break point corresponds approximately to 10, and the higher break point corresponds approximately to 1000. Reasoning: At low frequency, the slope changes from 0 to -20 dB/dec, indicating that there is a first-order pole at the lower break point, so the denominator contains (s+10). At high frequency, the slope changes from -20 dB/dec back to 0, indicating that there is a first-order zero at the higher break point, so the numerator contains (s+1000). Therefore the form is G(s)=K(s+1000)/(s+10). At high frequency, the magnitude of (s+1000)/(s+10) tends to 1, while the high-frequency asymptotic magnitude in the figure is -20 dB, that is, the magnitude is 0.1, so K=0.1. Low-frequency check: G(0)=0.1*1000/10=10, corresponding to 20 log10(10)=20 dB, consistent with the low-frequency plateau in the figure. Therefore G(s)=(s+1000)/(10(s+10)).

raw_record.question_text: A Bode magnitude plot for the transfer function \(G(s)\) of a plant is shown in the figure. What is the transfer function \(G(s)\) of the plant?

method.method_draft: First describe the image: it is a Bode magnitude plot of 20 log|G(j2πf)| versus logarithmic frequency, flat at +20 dB at low frequencies, then rolling downward, then flat at -20 dB at high frequencies. Infer a first-order pole at the lower corner because the slope changes from 0 to -20 dB/decade, and a first-order zero at the upper corner because the slope returns from -20 dB/decade to 0. Read the lower and upper corner values as corresponding to approximately 10 and 1000 in the s-domain scale. Write G(s)=K(s+1000)/(s+10). Use the high-frequency asymptote K=0.1, or equivalently use the low-frequency gain to verify 0.1·1000/10=10. Thus G(s)=(s+1000)/(10(s+10)).
method.CoT_raw:
图像描述：图中是一个 Bode 幅值图，纵轴标为 20 log|G(j2πf)|，横轴为对数频率 f(Hz)。曲线在低频段约为 +20 dB 的水平线；随后在较低拐点附近开始向下滚降；中间段呈约 -20 dB/dec 的下降趋势；在较高拐点之后又变为水平线，稳定在约 -20 dB。由图上横轴读数，较低拐点约对应 10，较高拐点约对应 1000。
推理：低频处斜率从 0 变为 -20 dB/dec，说明在较低拐点处有一个一阶极点，因此分母含有 (s+10)。高频处斜率从 -20 dB/dec 回到 0，说明在较高拐点处有一个一阶零点，因此分子含有 (s+1000)。所以形式为 G(s)=K(s+1000)/(s+10)。高频时 (s+1000)/(s+10) 的幅值趋近于 1，而图中高频渐近幅值为 -20 dB，即幅值为 0.1，所以 K=0.1。低频校验：G(0)=0.1*1000/10=10，对应 20 log10(10)=20 dB，与图中低频平台一致。因此 G(s)=(s+1000)/(10(s+10))。
